author: Pxx500
name: NHCogs
install_msg:
Thank you for installing NHCogs.
Load it with `[p]load NHCogs`.
short: NewHorizons utility and moderation cogs in one extension.
description: Loads ConsoleDump, NHMisc, Honeypot, Cleanup, GitHubTickets, NHModeration, and Custom Commands together while preserving their separate commands, configuration, and stored data
end_user_data_statement:
NHMisc stores Discord IDs needed for its activity, sticky-role, role-analytics, achievement, and operational error features.

Activity tracking stores user IDs with message counts for a configurable number of days. It also stores channel and thread IDs. Older daily summaries keep anonymous totals and channel IDs, but no user IDs.

Sticky roles store guild, user, and role IDs. Optional role analytics stores the current user IDs, bot flags, and role IDs for each enabled guild. Usernames and display names are used only when creating an export and are not saved.

Achievements store guild and user IDs, achievement keys and display names, optional bound role IDs, timestamps, state, and optional proof-message IDs. Gate increment also stores the source message, moderator, recipients, target roles, result message, and operation status. This prevents the same message from being processed twice and allows interrupted changes to resume. Message content and usernames are not saved.

Operational error records store the guild, source, action, short error summary, exception type, occurrence times and count, failure fingerprint, recovery state, and optional Discord location IDs. Tracebacks are sent only to the configured private Discord error channel and are not stored in SQLite.

Custom Commands stores guild IDs, command names and response content, response weights and order, cooldown settings, revisions, author and editor IDs and names, and create or edit timestamps. Its one-time migration keeps a JSON backup and validation report. User-data deletion replaces matching author and editor identity in the catalog, legacy configuration, and local migration artifacts while preserving command content and cooldowns. Ordinary user-data requests preserve configured access rules. Discord account deletion also redacts matching individual access IDs.

Bot Proxy stores character names and avatars, creator and updater IDs, active workflow IDs, published text, message locations, sender snapshots, and publication history in SQLite. User-data deletion removes characters created by the user and their saved avatars, closes their active sessions, and anonymizes matching updater, publisher, editor, and deleter attribution. Server-owned published messages, their content, and operational location IDs remain. Copies in exports or backups are not automatically erased.

User-data deletion removes that user's activity details, sticky roles, role-analytics records, and achievement history. Gate moderator and recipient IDs are anonymized, and pending awards for that user are removed. Completed operation details are cleared when it is safe to do so. Source-message locks and anonymous totals are retained to prevent duplicate processing.

Managed Cleanup commands do not create additional data.

Honeypot stores moderation case metadata about detected users and messages in SQLite and publishes a summary, thread timeline, and captured attachment copies to a configured Discord review channel. It also retains Gateway-observed message, guild, channel, and author IDs, timestamps, pin state, author kind, and optional one-way spam fingerprints for 14 days to support purge, spam detection, and managed cleanup; it stores no message content or attachments in that registry. Case evidence files are removed by resolution cleanup; the resolved Discord thread is locked and archived. Attachments selected as image-reference samples are copied to separate image-scan storage and remain until explicitly removed. The reference dataset has no automatic expiry and is not included in the case or user-data deletion described below. Ordinary user requests, including Red's strict-user mode, remove optional account and activity snapshots while preserving the moderation cases, evidence, reasons, IDs, timestamps, verification restrictions, and pending actions required for operation. Explicit owner or deleted-account requests retain the stronger deletion path. These requests do not unban anyone. Guild removal follows the existing case and registry cleanup path. Channel and thread deletion removes matching registry rows. Unavailable Discord case deletions remain queued for retry. During a temporary loss of Message Content, enabled moderation queues observed guild, channel, and message IDs with times and retry state for up to 14 days. It stores no message text or attachments in that queue. After access returns, it fetches only those known messages and reprocesses them. Events never delivered by Discord and already deleted content cannot be reconstructed.

NHModeration stores source observations and canonical moderation actions in SQLite. Observations may contain guild, target, technical executor, credited moderator, and channel IDs, action type, timestamps, reasons, expiry, source identity, migration run identity, and attribution hints. It also stores synchronization cursors, migration state, and operational failure records. Ordinary user and strict-user requests remove optional target account and activity snapshots while preserving necessary moderation reasons, identifiers, and history. Explicit owner or deleted-account requests anonymize matching identities and reasons, then rebuild affected projections. Guild removal deletes that guild's history, synchronization state, migration state, failures, and configuration.

GitHubTickets stores guild and user IDs, optional GitHub usernames, expertise categories, pull request titles and links, Discord ticket locations, reviewer routing state, exclusions, reviewer presence tiers at notification time, ping history, and deadlines in SQLite. Finished tickets, deleted ticket messages or threads, guild removal, and Red user-data deletion remove the corresponding data. Discord message content is not read back into the database.
